focus.jnote: The scanner boarded ZERO names, and the tape is a correction trying to bounce with the VIX still above 30 — that combination is the whole story. On Friday the S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39, down 3.70%, the Dow closed at 48,147.33, down 1.93%, and the Nasdaq closed at 22,617.73, down 5.28%. It was the seventh straight daily loss, leaving the index more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record, officially in a correction. The fear gauge spiked: the VIX closed at 35.89, up 26.20% from Thursday, and briefly reached 40.03 during the session. This morning is a relief attempt — futures are bouncing: S&P 500 +2.1%, Nasdaq 100 +3.0%, Dow +1.4%. But the VIX remained at its highest level since the ‘Liberation Day’ tariff announcement in 2025. A Sniper does not sell premium into a bounce off a correction low while vol is this stretched — and today there is literally nothing on the board to take.
focus.notdown: There is no clean ‘Not-Down’ name today. The scanner’s Type A (earnings), Type B (news) and Type C (breakout) passes all finished with zero boarded. A ~2% futures bounce after seven down days is the textbook oversold snap-back, but in a VIX-above-30 correction those bounces are violent and two-sided — exactly where a bull put gets run over on the next down-leg. Watch-only; sell nothing.
focus.notup: There is no clean ‘Not-Up’ name either. Selling bear calls into a sharp relief rally off a correction low is its own trap — futures rose over 2% following seven straight days of declines, and any squeeze on short-covering gaps a bear call the wrong way fast. With a Dec 9 Fed hike nearly priced and the tape whipsawing on every headline, the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three things stack. One: composite 74 is HOT and P(≥1% gap) at ~52% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. Two: the S&P just entered a correction on a seventh straight loss with the VIX closing at 35.89 (~40 intraday) and a December 9 Fed hike nearly fully priced — a stretched, two-sided tape where today’s ~2% bounce can reverse just as fast. Three: the full-universe scanner ran and boarded ZERO names — no Type A, B or C setup qualified, and the rules forbid inventing one. Stand down on new credit spreads, keep any existing DTE clear of the Dec 9 FOMC, and re-run tomorrow. Cash is a position today.
